tool.name: qpcrpredict
tool.description: trained positive/negative calls from raw real-time PCR run files (.eds, .rdml)
tool.command: ## the format is detected from the file content, the link only keeps a readable name in the report ln -s '$run' 'run_file' && qpcrpredict predict --run 'run_file' #if str($assay_source.source) == 'packaged' --target '$assay_source.target' #else --target '$assay_source.target_name' --assay '$assay_source.assay' #end if #if str($model_source.source) == 'history' --model '$model_source.model' #end if #if str($sample).strip() != '' --sample '$sample' #end if --out '$predictions' --quiet

param.name: run
param.label: qPCR run file (.eds or .rdml)
param.help: One run file: an Applied Biosystems .eds project file, or an RDML file as exported by most qPCR software. The format is detected from the content.

param.name: source
param.label: Assay
param.help: The assay configuration defines the targets, the reference gene, the control names and the thresholds. Use the packaged AML MRD assay, or supply your own configuration (JSON, see 'qpcrpredict assay --show generic').
param.option: Packaged assay: AML molecular MRD (reference ABL1)

param.name: target
param.label: Target
param.help: The tool reads the replicate wells of this target and the reference wells of the same sample.

param.name: target_name
param.label: Target
param.help: A target name or alias of the assay, or the detector name as written on the plate.

param.name: source
param.label: Prediction model
param.help: Use the model shipped with the tool (trained for the packaged AML MRD assay), or supply a bundle trained with 'qpcrpredict train'. A model from the history is required for any other assay.

param.name: model
param.label: Trained model bundle (.pkl)
param.help: Model bundles are pickle files. Only use bundles from a source you trust.

param.name: sample
param.label: Single sample (optional)
param.help: Leave empty to score every sample that carries the target in the run, or give one sample name.

tool.help:
**What it does**
``qpcrpredict`` is part of the LeukoPredict tools. It predicts the **positive** or **negative** call of a qPCR assay directly from the raw run file. Only the instrument data are used: the shape of the amplification curves and the Ct and quantity of the selected target and of the reference gene of the same sample. A quality and review gate turns runs that cannot be evaluated into an explicit **na** (repeat) decision and borderline cases into a **review** flag for human classification.
The packaged model was trained for AML molecular measurable residual disease (mutated NPM1, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11, PML::RARA and BCR::ABL1, normalised to ABL1). For any other assay, supply your own assay configuration and a model trained with ``qpcrpredict train``.
**Inputs**
* *qPCR run file* - an Applied Biosystems ``.eds`` file or an RDML file. * *Assay* - the packaged AML MRD assay, or an assay configuration (JSON) from the history. * *Target* - the target to score. * *Prediction model* - the packaged model, or a bundle trained with ``qpcrpredict train``. * *Single sample* (optional) - restrict scoring to one sample.
**Output**
A tabular file with one row per sample: the ``decision`` (positive / negative / review / na), the call and probability of the model, the material quality, the key readouts (target Ct, reference copies, standard-curve R2, target/reference ratio) and the reason and recommendation for every deferred sample.
**Note**
The output supports the decision and does not replace expert review of the amplification curves, in particular for low-level and borderline cases, which the tool flags as *review*.
